findings.issue_text: [Medium/security] The domain restriction regex `@(#{domains})` in lib/validators/email_validator.rb:20 is unanchored, so a whitelist entry like `allowed.com` also matches `user@allowed.com.evil.com` — attacker-controlled subdomains pass the whitelist (and blacklist entries over-block subdomain-suffixed addresses); anchor the match to the domain part (e.g. `/\A[^@]+@(?:#{domains})\z/`)

[Medium/security] `where(email: email)` in app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 is an exact, case-sensitive match and neither stored blocklist entries nor the submitted address are normalized, so blocking is trivially bypassed with case/whitespace variants ("Foo@Spam.com" vs "foo@spam.com"); downcase/strip on both write and lookup (or query `lower(email) = ?`)

[Low/performance] Validation now has DB write side effects: every User validation with a changed email issues a `blocked_emails` SELECT, and on a match an UPDATE that re-runs BlockedEmail's own validations (another uniqueness query); `valid?` should be side-effect free — separate the pure check from attempt tracking

[Low/concurrency] `match_count += 1` followed by `save` in app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16 is a non-atomic read-modify-write; concurrent registration attempts with the same blocked email lose increments; use an atomic `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = :now")`

[Low/security] The structured `errors` payload plus the distinct `user.email.blocked` message in app/controllers/users_controller.rb:198 gives a clean oracle to probe which specific email addresses are on the blocklist; use a generic message and/or rate-limit registration attempts

[Low/bug] A blocked-but-syntactically-valid email is reported inline with the generic `user.email.invalid` reason in create_account_controller.js:69-74; the server's specific message is discarded for the field-level validation, which misleads the user

[Low/bug] Any email error (e.g. "has already been taken") pushes the address into `rejectedEmails` (create_account_controller.js:272-273), which is never cleared/reset, so the address is flagged invalid client-side for the rest of the session even after the server-side condition changes (e.g. blocklist entry removed, email freed)

[Low/bug] The validator wired as `validates :email, email: true` (user.rb:47) performs no format check despite its name/wiring; syntactically invalid addresses ("notanemail") pass when no domain whitelist/blacklist is configured since the client-side check is bypassable via the API; verify and add a format check + spec

[Low/test_gap] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb only exercises the stubbed `BlockedEmail.should_block?` branch; the whitelist/blacklist restriction logic moved out of user.rb has no cases (whitelist pass/fail, blacklist match, or that a domain error short-circuits the blocklist lookup)

[Low/test_gap] No spec covers the new `errors`/`values` JSON payload in app/controllers/users_controller.rb:196-201, and there is no end-to-end test that registering a blocklisted email fails via the User model with the `user.email.blocked` message (the User↔EmailValidator wiring is untested)

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] `match_count += 1` followed by `save` in app/models/blocked_email.rb:14-16 is a non-atomic read-modify-write; concurrent registration attempts with the same blocked email lose increments; use an atomic `update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = :now")`

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?` the code does `record.match_count += 1` then `record.save` (lines 14-16). This is a non-atomic read/modify/write on a shared counter; concurrent calls matching the same `blocked_emails.email` can overwrite each other and lose increments, causing incorrect `match_count` statistics (data loss) and potentially inaccurate `last_match_at` updates. An atomic update (e.g., `update_all`/`update_counters`) would avoid this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new, distinct validation error for blocked emails (`I18n.t(:'user.email.blocked')` in `lib/validators/email_validator.rb`) and exposes structured per-field errors plus echoed input values in the registration failure response (`errors: user.errors.to_hash, values: ... slice("...", "email")` in `app/controllers/users_controller.rb`). Together, an unauthenticated caller can submit registration attempts and reliably distinguish “blocked email” from other failures, effectively probing whether a specific address is on the `blocked_emails` list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] A blocked-but-syntactically-valid email is reported inline with the generic `user.email.invalid` reason in create_account_controller.js:69-74; the server's specific message is discarded for the field-level validation, which misleads the user

adjudication.rationale: In `create_account_controller.js`, when an email has been rejected by the server and is later re-entered, the new `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` branch returns a failed `Discourse.InputValidation` with `reason: I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` (generic) rather than using the server-provided field error (e.g. `user.email.blocked` from `EmailValidator`). The server now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and the validator adds a specific `user.email.blocked` message, but the client only caches the rejected value and replays it as `user.email.invalid`, which can mislead for blocked-but-syntactically-valid emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] Any email error (e.g. "has already been taken") pushes the address into `rejectedEmails` (create_account_controller.js:272-273), which is never cleared/reset, so the address is flagged invalid client-side for the rest of the session even after the server-side condition changes (e.g. blocklist entry removed, email freed)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `rejectedEmails` as a persistent array on the controller (`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])`) and the email validation short-circuits to failure if the current email is contained in it. On account-create failure, the code pushes the submitted email whenever `result.errors.email` is present (`if (result.errors && result.errors.email && result.values) { ...pushObject(result.values.email); }`), which would include non-“blocked” cases like “taken”. There is no corresponding reset/clear of `rejectedEmails` shown in this diff, so within the lifetime of that controller instance the same address will be permanently treated as invalid client-side even if the server-side reason changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] The validator wired as `validates :email, email: true` (user.rb:47) performs no format check despite its name/wiring; syntactically invalid addresses ("notanemail") pass when no domain whitelist/blacklist is configured since the client-side check is bypassable via the API; verify and add a format check + spec

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmailValidator` added in `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` only enforces whitelist/blacklist and `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, and `User` now wires it via `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`. There is indeed no syntactic/format validation in this validator, so values like `"notanemail"` would not be rejected when no domain restrictions are configured and the email isn’t blocked. However, this diff also removes an earlier `email_validator` method that likewise only enforced whitelist/blacklist (no format check either), so this is not clearly a defect introduced by the PR—more a (potentially important) missing validation/enhancement and naming mismatch than a verifiable regression caused by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb only exercises the stubbed `BlockedEmail.should_block?` branch; the whitelist/blacklist restriction logic moved out of user.rb has no cases (whitelist pass/fail, blacklist match, or that a domain error short-circuits the blocklist lookup)

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmailValidator` contains nontrivial domain whitelist/blacklist logic (copied from `User#email_validator`) plus a short-circuit before calling `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (`if record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`). However, `spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb` only covers the blocked-email behavior by stubbing `BlockedEmail.should_block?` true/false, and does not add cases for whitelist pass/fail, blacklist match/non-match, or asserting that a domain restriction error prevents the blocked-email lookup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] No spec covers the new `errors`/`values` JSON payload in app/controllers/users_controller.rb:196-201, and there is no end-to-end test that registering a blocklisted email fails via the User model with the `user.email.blocked` message (the User↔EmailValidator wiring is untested)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in `UsersController#create` to render `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` on failure, but no controller/request spec is shown to assert this new JSON payload. Separately, while there are unit specs for `EmailValidator` and `BlockedEmail`, there is no spec demonstrating the `User` model’s `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` wiring produces the `user.email.blocked` error during registration (i.e., end-to-end through `User` validation / controller create path). This is a concrete test coverage gap introduced by the new logic, not a verified runtime defect.
